scene: At the very bottom of the abyss, show the young apprentice taking one careful step from a muddy bank toward a shallow black toxic swamp. Composition at ankle height: foreground leather boot and embroidered black cloak edge at LEFT, vast corrupt dark water and ragged reeds opening across the center and right into green poisonous mist, wet cave rock above, no open sky. A small warm lantern partly visible. Not the discovery of a splint or note, no kneeling or map. The swamp water itself is the main subject, oppressive and still. Exactly one apprentice, only natural body parts.

The discarded unfinished wooden vessels, Morden's failed brothers, in the subterranean swamp. New composition from INSIDE the heap, looking through the hollow ribs of one abandoned wooden torso at row upon row of unfinished wooden human-shaped faces and torsos half submerged in mud. Strong foreground framing, every body visibly carved wood, black iron joints, abandoned empty sockets rather than human corpses. A diagonal cold shaft of light shows the huge number beyond. NO living characters, no apprentice, no Morden, no palace, no giant hero atop the heap. No visible crest required. Somber compassion rather than horror spectacle.

View from WITHIN dense tall black reeds at water level, looking far across the poisonous underground swamp to one very small warm amber light on a low island in thick green-grey mist. Reeds almost conceal the island; their layered silhouettes lead the eye to the lamp, which is the only warm point. A dark cavern roof barely visible high above. No characters, no notes, no map, no palace. A mysterious surviving light at the bottom of poison, not a comfortable populated village.

Historical memory of the very frail old first soul-binder's last instruction to the one finished wooden vessel, Morden, inside the swamp island workshop. New intimate composition: close view of the founder's weak, wrinkled hand extended from a dark embroidered sleeve on the LEFT, resting on the receptive wooden hand of Morden on the RIGHT. The edge of the founder's long white hair and downward face is softly visible at extreme left; Morden's pale gaunt unaging face is partly cropped at upper right, attentive and sorrowful, wearing the plain workshop clothes from the reference memory, no ceremonial hat. The hands are the center; exact natural five fingers per hand, clearly wooden grain on Morden. Muted blue-green swamp light outside and one dim warm work candle. NO text, no elaborate crest, no king, no palace, no present-day apprentice. Not evil villain origin: a desperate request passed to someone who wants to protect souls.

A monumental storm tower rising UP from the abyss. View almost vertically upward from its dark wet base in the subterranean swamp: spiral stone stairs wrap around the tower, enormous hanging chains sweep from lower foreground to disappearing heights, storm light white-blue at the far upper opening. A tiny distant black-and-gold apprentice climbing one stair gives scale but is not foreground. Strong spiraling ascent, no broken staff discovery, no kneeling, no maps, no palace, no king. Distinct from ordinary ruined castle exterior; tower is impossibly tall inside the abyss.

Inside the mouth of one enormous bronze bell in the storm tower, looking OUT through its dark curved rim into a narrow slit of turbulent storm clouds. The massive bell clapper looms at the left, one tiny pale-cyan soul flame rises toward the cloud gap at the center-right. Dynamic diagonal bell rim suggests the bell has just sounded. Intricate worn bronze and small unrecognizable ornament, no readable letters or invented crest, no human characters, no maps, no palace. Main contrast is dark metal against a single fragile escaping light; not a close-up discovery of an inscription.

The exterior stone walkway of the storm tower viewed across a deep vertical chasm from the opposite wall. Tiny cyan soul lights and violent white-blue lightning are drawn along huge taut chains toward the upper tower structures, the circulation visibly constrained, without diagram arrows. Jagged wet stone walkway cuts diagonally through the center; storm darkness and rain stream around it. No apprentice taking notes, no rod closeup, no maps, no palace or king, no legible text, no friendly living settlement. The chains and trapped current are the focal point, huge architecture oppressive.

A vast ancient prison transport bridge above a brilliant WHITE CLOUD SEA in clear bright BLUE DAYLIGHT. New panoramic long shot from the SIDE, not from along the walkway: the narrow stone bridge stretches nearly horizontally across the middle, connecting a storm tower edge at left to the immense empty ruined arena city at right. One tiny brown-haired black-and-gold cloaked apprentice with a brown satchel walks at center to establish scale. Iron restraints/rings on the bridge hint at its cruel past. Bright open sky, no storm clouds, no heavy dark sky. No closeup glove, no kneeling, no palace, no king. The exhilarating openness and harsh bridge are the subject.

Historical memory of the arena's soul reuse, viewed from INSIDE an empty battered fighter's cage through heavy iron bars. Foreground shows a broken empty wooden articulated gladiator body slumped near the bars; beyond, on a plain workbench, a single cyan soul-light in a brass lantern stands beside another empty wooden fighter body awaiting use, its chest access panel open. Rows of similar unlit lanterns recede dimly. No gore, no human corpses, clearly carved wooden bodies with iron joints. No living technician needs to be depicted; this quiet arrangement explains the repeated use without diagrams or text. Amber arena firelight far beyond, cold cyan soul flame focal. No apprentice examining shelves, no palace or king.
